parsed.explanation: Combined regime: national criminal law, document rules and custody apply directly on the island. The documented national detention picture is the gravest exposure — the 2021 watchdog opinion records serious rights violations against trans persons in deprivation of liberty across ~40 referrals since 2010, an unremedied recurring finding (rule 11: oversight repetition corroborates exposure, not mitigation), though prison placement rules at least weigh best interests and individual-cell options. No island-specific violence, policing, border-document or care denial is documented; local signals are positive and recent: a first LGBT+ centre (2024), a minister announcing adapted anti-discrimination measures, and a 2025 community event calendar. These are climate signals and thin community infrastructure, not operative visitor protections. No criminalisation of gender expression appears. A visitor outed faces a custody system with documented, unremedied trans-specific violations, but everyday exposure (border, services, street) shows no documented hostility and some documented acceptance. Sites above the 0.65 anchors' incident-based tier only marginally and below the 0.75 protective-regime tier, for the custody gap and the thin local evidence base.

entry_documents.protection: National identity-document rules apply; no island- or record-documented friction for foreign trans documents at entry.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening is nationally set; no mismatch-based refusals or secondary-screening pattern appears in the dossier.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National detention rules apply on the island; watchdog found serious fundamental-rights violations against trans persons in detention, recurring since 2010 (~40 referrals), unremedied. Placement follows legal gender, with best-interest weighing, individual cells, or placement with men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Placement guidance weighing best interests and individual-cell options partially mitigates; watchdog monitoring exists.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any investigation/detention (e.g. document dispute) routes into the national custodial system whose violations the watchdog corroborates.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prison placement by legal gender may mismatch presentation; detention-ward and other facility conditions not island-documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Best-interest weighing and single-cell placement are documented national practice.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National prison rules carry directly to the island; island operates no separate regime.

care_services.protection: First LGBT+ centre (2024) offers reception, support and orientation; national minister announced anti-discrimination measures adapted for overseas territories.
care_services.interaction: Centre is resident/community-facing; delivery of national measures shaped by distance from national administration.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No island-specific policing data; no criminalisation of gender expression documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National ministerial commitment to fighting gender-based violence and discrimination on the island, framed for overseas territories.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National law-enforcement framework applies; island practice unrecorded.

minors_guardians.protection: Community centre and 2025 social-event calendar are open community infrastructure; no age-specific rules documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No island-specific anti-trans violence or policing data identified — a record gap, not a finding of safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Growing community acceptance reported (2023 interview); activism advancing.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: National policing framework applies; local response untested by evidence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Watchdog findings persisted for over a decade without documented remedy; island violence, healthcare and police data absent; local-variation data missing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National preventive mechanism exists and referred cases; centre and ministerial measures are recent institutional positives.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Oversight repetition corroborates exposure rather than offsetting it (rule 11); thin data prevents confidence in either direction.

anchor_checks.comparison: Materially safer than 0.35-A: no visitor register, no entry exclusion, no discretionary removal mechanism documented; the island has no visitor-facing restriction at all, whereas 0.35-A's exposure is universal and border-enforced.

Comparable-to-slightly-above 0.55-C: no documented ward-placement or care-denial regime locally; the documented national custody-violation record is the main weight, similar in kind to 0.55-C's institutional friction but with documented serious violations and thinner local evidence.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor shows functioning, remedied border/custody handling (counsel, compensation, written reasons); here the national watchdog documents persistent unremedied violations against trans detainees, and no working island-level remedy is documented.

Slightly above 0.65-A: no documented checkpoint outing incident locally, positive recent community infrastructure and ministerial measures; but the custody backdrop is worse than 0.65-A's accountable-release pattern, capping the score near the band boundary.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is the governing state's: criminal law, documents, custody and the preventive mechanism all carry directly to the island, which adds no hostile layer of its own. The one documented exposure is custodial — a decade of watchdog findings of serious violations against trans persons in detention, unremedied, which under rule 11 corroborates rather than mitigates risk; it activates only if a visitor is detained, so it weighs materially but not overwhelmingly. Against this sit recent, documented local positives — the island's first LGBT+ centre with national ministerial backing, adapted anti-discrimination measures, and a growing community calendar — plus no documented criminalisation, border friction, facility bans or street violence. The evidence base is thin: silence on island policing and violence is a record gap, not proof of safety, but the structural signals (no criminal statute, protective national framing, community infrastructure) resolve the unknowns toward moderate safety. Site: low Reduced Risk, ~0.66, held below the 0.75 tier by the unremedied custody record and evidentiary gaps.
